LESSON: BALAAM’S DONKEY

Grade: Grade 4
Subject: CHRISTIAN RELIGIOUS EDUCATION
Strand: The Holy Bible
Topic 2.3: Balaam’s Donkey

SECTION 1: WELCOME

Hello! This is a study lesson on Balaam’s Donkey. Read the explanation, follow every worked example, then do the practice. This is original CBC Learn content written from KICD outcomes — not a copy of a commercial textbook.

Big question: Why did the donkey talk?

SECTION 2: WHAT YOU WILL LEARN

By the end of this lesson, you will be able to:

1. retell the story of Balaam and his donkey
2. apply the story in their lives by obeying God’s instructions

SECTION 3: STUDY NOTES (READ AND LEARN)

WHAT YOU ARE STUDYING: BALAAM’S DONKEY
Subject: CHRISTIAN RELIGIOUS EDUCATION · Grade: Grade 4
This is a learner study lesson (not a teacher guide). Read every part, follow the models, then practise.

BIG PICTURE
Balaam’s Donkey helps you succeed in CHRISTIAN RELIGIOUS EDUCATION. You will understand it, practise it, and use it at home, at your place of worship, and at school.

KEY FACTS: BALAAM’S DONKEY
Study Balaam’s Donkey like a learner textbook page: meaning → examples → practice → check.
Replace teacher words with your own words.
If a step is unclear, rewrite it shorter and try again.

PART 1: Retell the story of Balaam and his donkey

What this means
In this part you learn to retell the story of Balaam and his donkey. You will use ideas from at home, at your place of worship, and at school.

How to learn it
1. Read the idea carefully: retell the story of Balaam and his donkey.
2. Reflect, retell, then practise a good habit using a Kenyan example from your life.
3. Check yourself: Can you explain it without looking?

Model
Value in action: Show how “Balaam’s Donkey” looks when you treat a classmate kindly.

Your turn
Do one short practice that proves you can retell the story of Balaam and his donkey. Write or say your answer clearly.

PART 2: Apply the story in their lives by obeying God’s instructions

What this means
In this part you learn to apply the story in their lives by obeying God’s instructions. You will use ideas from at home, at your place of worship, and at school.

How to learn it
1. Read the idea carefully: apply the story in their lives by obeying God’s instructions.
2. Reflect, retell, then practise a good habit using a Kenyan example from your life.
3. Check yourself: Can you explain it without looking?

Model
Story link: Retell a short faith/values story connected to Balaam’s Donkey in your own words.

Your turn
Do one short practice that proves you can apply the story in their lives by obeying God’s instructions. Write or say your answer clearly.

PUT IT TOGETHER
Close your notes and say aloud: what Balaam’s Donkey is, one example, and one way you will practise this week.

SECTION 4: QUICK EXAMPLES

Example 1: Show how “Balaam’s Donkey” looks when you treat a classmate kindly. (skill: retell the story of Balaam and his donkey)

Example 2: Retell a short faith/values story connected to Balaam’s Donkey in your own words. (skill: apply the story in their lives by obeying God’s instructions)

SECTION 5: PRACTICE NOW

1. Write 5 sentences (or show 5 clear steps) that teach Balaam’s Donkey to a classmate.
2. Practise this skill: retell the story of Balaam and his donkey.
3. Practise this skill: apply the story in their lives by obeying God’s instructions.
4. Make one local Kenya example of Balaam’s Donkey from your county, market, farm, or school.
5. Mark your own work: What did you get right? What will you redo?

SECTION 6: WORK TO DO (HOME / REVISION)

1. In your exercise book, make a one-page revision sheet for Balaam’s Donkey: meaning, 3 examples, 5 practice items.
2. Teach a parent/guardian or younger sibling one part of this lesson (2 minutes).
3. Answer in writing: Why should a Grade 4 learner study Balaam’s Donkey?
4. Prepare for the quiz: cover the Remember box and recite it.

SECTION: THINK ABOUT IT

1. Why did the donkey talk?

SECTION: REMEMBER

1. Know what Balaam’s Donkey means in your own words.
2. Use local Kenyan examples, not only definitions.
3. Practise in small steps, then check your work.
4. Be able to: retell the story of Balaam and his donkey.
5. Be able to: apply the story in their lives by obeying God’s instructions.

Now complete the Revision Quiz. Open Answers only after you finish.

— CBC Learn · Original study notes from KICD outcomes (Strategy 2)
